description: Totals from the Migrant Program Money Register, built from USAspending award records, HHS's TAGGS terminated-grants list and the IRS Exempt Organizations Business Master File: federal obligations, FY2023 to FY2026, to the organisations and governments that shelter, care for, resettle, transport and give legal help to migrants and refugees, in eight programs keyed from the award ID (ORR unaccompanied-children grants and ORR contracts, ORR refugee formula, Matching Grant and discretionary grants, State Department Reception and Placement, FEMA's Shelter and Services Program and DOJ EOIR legal access). Returns the all-programs total with its basis; money by program and fiscal year, with net obligations, positive obligations and de-obligations labelled; the equal twelve-month windows either side of January 20, 2025; recipient-class shares by program and year, with state, local and tribal governments apart from organisations and organisations split by IRS match; FEMA's Shelter and Services de-obligations of February 10 to 12, 2025 (the record gives no reason), with the government share; termination records counted by agency and record type; withheld recipients and records as counts and amounts; the exclusions, the awards placed outside the United States listed with their amounts; and the register's headlines with their basis. Awards whose record places the work outside the United States are excluded from every figure, as are FEMA's Emergency Food and Shelter Program and ICE detention money. Every amount is an obligation from the award records (the government's commitment to pay), net of de-obligations, by action date; net obligations, positive obligations and de-obligations are separate stages, each labelled with its fiscal year and the as-of date, award-level outlays (only where the record carries them) are the record's cumulative figure to the as-of date, and they are never added across stages. Governments are kept apart from organisations: every amount names its recipient class from the register's reviewed table, never a single NGO total. A recipient is called an IRS-listed exempt organisation only where the register's IRS EO BMF match stands (by the reviewed EIN, or by exact name and state where the register marks the match by rule), shown with that record; other organisations read organisation, IRS status not matched. The tools never call a recipient nonprofit or faith-based, and no recipient is classified by religion. Terminations appear only in the agency's exact words with their dates; where the record gives no words the answer says the record gives no reason, and an executive-order tag appears only as the record shows it. Lobbying reports (LDA), connected PACs (FEC), ICE and CBP contracts (the Pay-to-Play Register, where ICE detention sits) and super PAC gifts (the Super PAC Donors Register) are side columns: shown side by side, never added to program money and never put in date sequence with an award or a termination. Every answer carries the register's question note: these records show federal awards and the agencies' own termination records; they do not show how any recipient used the money or why an award was made or ended beyond what the record says. Every answer also carries the side-by-side caption, the as-of and retrieval dates, each file's date, the source page on morvs.ai and the licence. Institutions only: no beneficiary, staff member, executive or sole proprietor is named; withheld recipients and records appear only as counts and amounts.
